newsitem.title: JAPAN: High Dubai price seen sustained - Japan oil chief.
newsitem.headline: High Dubai price seen sustained - Japan oil chief.

text.p: The price of Dubai crude is expected to hover around $20 per barrel for a while as factors to push prices down are unlikely to emerge in the short term, the head of an oil industry body said on Wednesday.
"Dubai crude above $20 is far too high, however, prices are likely to move around $20 in the short term," Yuji Idemitsu, chairman of the Petroleum Association of Japan (PAJ), said.
He said U.S. and European oil firms' policy of keeping oil product stockpiles low in order to cut costs would support the market, but that another spike in prices was unlikely in the near future.

The price of Dubai crude, regarded as a benchmark crude in Asia, jumped above $20 on September 3 in response to heightening tension between the United States and Iraq. The Middle East crude has been priced below $19 in the past year.
Idemitsu said the fundamental supply/demand situation had not changed, in spite of recent developments involving Iraq and the United States. "Crude supplies are not tight," he said.

Idemitsu also said he was very worried about domestic gasoline retail prices, which have been falling in spite of rising crude markets. "Price cutting competition among gasoline stations is spreading," he said.
